title: KV: page-consolidation and proactive rebalancer to reduce paging and slot churn
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: On long-lived workloads with variable sequence lengths we observed sustained small-object allocations inside the KV arena that caused increased page faults, allocator metadata churn, and elevated tail latency during traffic spikes. This PR introduces a low-risk two-part approach: (1) a page-consolidation pass that coalesces small adjacent KV entries into contiguous pages to reduce fragmentation and the number of page table entries; (2) a proactive rebalancer that migrates underutilized slab regions between arenas during idle windows to keep hot entries collocated and free large contiguous ranges for future large-key allocations. Both changes are designed to be conservative by default (config flags + safe thresholds) and opt-in for Dedicated/Private customers before we flip to default in hosted environments.

What this PR does: Implements a background page-consolidation job in runtime/kv that runs opportunistically when CPU and memory headroom are available, and a proactive rebalancer in runtime/kv/rebalancer that uses a lightweight access-frequency sketch to move cold regions. The consolidation pass uses a compacting writer that preserves existing stable pointers for readers via a short-lived epoch grace period (readers observe old pages until consolidation completes). The rebalancer integrates with scheduler to request small maintenance windows (micro-backoff) so migration does not interfere with latency SLOs.

Compatibility and safety: All behavior gated behind config flags (kvc.page_consolidation.enabled, kvc.rebalancer.enabled) with thresholds and a rollout knob (max_migrations_per_minute). The data movement maintains checksums and uses write-ahead markers so we can resume interrupted consolidations after process restart. No on-disk format changes.

Benchmarks: On a synthetic chat workload (p50 token latency-sensitive, mixed short/long sequences) we measured: - 9-12% reduction in page-faults per-minute; - 6% improvement in sustained throughput at SLO latency windows under high concurrency; - 18% reduction in tail latency spikes attributable to paging-related stalls. Overhead when idle is <1% CPU; consolidation triggered ~2x per hour on the test fixture.

Testing and rollout: Unit + integration tests added for consolidation correctness and rebalancer anti-starvation. End-to-end perf lab runs and canary on internal Dedicated cluster for 48h before broader rollout. Feature flags will be used to gradually enable across tenant tiers.

Related: ENG-5801 (KV reliability epic), ENG-6020 (scheduler maintenance windows), PERF-128 (bench harness updates).

release_notes: Introduces an opt-in KV page consolidation pass and proactive rebalancer to reduce fragmentation and paging. Expected to reduce page-fault related tail latency and improve throughput for mixed-length workloads. Disabled by default for Hosted; enable via kvc.page_consolidation.enabled and kvc.rebalancer.enabled in Dedicated/Private deployments.
notes: This PR intentionally avoids changing on-disk formats and keeps all behavior behind flags. Follow-up work: automated tuning of thresholds via Optimize recommendations and a telemetry signal to auto-suggest enabling to tenants that show high small-object churn.
